Commentary.Commentary: The visitors were good in the field. Roach and Gabriel bowled well with both the new balls and took wickets. Bishoo was wayward to begin with but settled into a rhythm to reach the landmark of 100 wickets in Test cricket. They will be pleased having restricted the home side under 350. There are no real demons on the track but it is taking slow turn and there is movement for the pace bowlers. Let's see how the Windies reply with the bat...

A fairly good show from Zimbabwe after electing to bat. To begin with, it was a horrid start for them as they lost three wickets for only 14. In came Peter Moor and along with Hamilton Masakadza steadied the ship for the home side. The duo stitched a 142-run stand and played sensible cricket. Masakadza, was given a life when he was on 15 by Gabriel and he made it count by scoring a big ton while Moor, who came in as a replacement scored a patient fifty. There was a bit of stutter this morning but once again Sikandar Raza stood tall. He took it on him and played an enterprising knock to take the hosts past 300, thereby becoming the leading run-scorer for his side in Tests this year.

OUT! No inside edge and Chisoro is a goner! Roach comes from around the wicket and bowls a slower ball on a full length on leg stump. Chisoro looks to keep it out but is hit on the boot. The Windies appeal in unison and up goes the umpire's finger. Tendai decides to challenge the decision. Time for the replays. It shows three reds and the debutant is a dead duck. Surprisingly, the Hawk Eye revealed that the ball pitched on leg stump and deviated in to hit the middle stump. Not quite sure how that's possible but in any case, ZIMBABWE ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 326.
Chisoro has been adjudged LBW. He takes the review straightaway. Is there an inside edge?
FOUR! Nicely done! Fuller length ball outside off, Mpofu pushes it with an angled bat face past the second slip fielder for a boundary.

A loud shout for a caught behind denied! Fullish delivery outside off, Mpofu pokes at it but gets beaten. Gabriel roars in an appeal but the umpire stays put. The replays show there was clear daylight between bat and ball.
Short delivery down the leg side, helped along with a pull to fine leg for a run.
Full delivery on off, Chisoro heaves it off the inner half to deep mid-wicket for a couple.
Chris Mpofu is the last man in.

OUT! Bull's eye brings the downfall of Cremer! Full length delivery, Graeme drives it crisply towards mid off and sets off for a run. He takes on the arm of his counterpart, Holder who is very quick to attack the ball. He moves to his left, picks it up cleanly and scores a direct hit at the bowler's end as Cremer tries to get in desperately. It is referred upstairs. The replays find the Zimbabwean skipper short of his crease. He took the longer route to avoid the throw and that proved to be his undoing.
Direct hits are always close and Holder believes that he has his man. Great work from the skipper and it's taken upstairs. Cremer seems to be struggling here...

Uppish but safe! Fullish delivery around off, Chisoro drives it with minimal foot movement in the gap between mid off and extra cover. A run taken. This time Cremer wanted the second but was sent back.
Fullish delivery, tailing in. Cremer works it to mid-wicket.
That was a loose shot! Short and room on offer, Cremer flashes at it but gets beaten.
Shaping in from a length outside off, Cremer leaves it alone and the ball goes past the off stump.
Fullish delivery, defended off the front foot.

What was the skipper doing there? That was a schoolboy error which almost proved fatal. Roach goes around the wicket and bowls a fuller length ball outside off, Chisoro plays it off the outer half towards gully and sets off initially. Cremer keeps running and the debutant has to eventually go for the run. Gabriel goes to his right and has a shy at the striker's end but misses. The replays show that in an attempt to avoid the throw, he took his eyes off the ball and was airborne. A direct hit would have sent him packing.
Roach goes wider of the crease and angles in a fullish delivery on off. Cremer pushes at it tentatively and gets it off the inner half through backward square leg. A run taken.
Bowls a very full delivery, attacking the base of off stump. Chisoro keeps it out to the mid-wicket region.
Gabriel comes from around the wicket and bowls a pacy full length delivery outside off, Tendai plants his front foot across and lets it sail into the gloves of the keeper.
Full length ball on middle, Chisoro drives it towards mid on. The fielder attacks the ball and denies the single.
Short delivery down the leg side, doesn't rise as much as expected. Tendai doesn't commit himself to the hook shot and hence, misses it.
Length delivery around off, Chisoro hangs back and buries it into the track.
Full length ball just outside off, Chisoro strides ahead and plays it with soft hands to covers.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, Cremer taps it to the fielder at mid on.
Good length ball around off, defended solidly off the back foot.
Length delivery in line of the stumps, Graeme tucks it to mid-wicket and wants a run but is rightly sent back.
Back of a length delivery around off, Graeme places it to backward point.
Very full delivery, tailing in. Cremer keeps it out towards Roach.
On a good length, shaping in. Cremer works it through backward square leg for a couple.
Fuller in length around off, pushed off the front foot to the cover region. End of a productive over for Gabriel.
Full delivery outside off, Tendai leaves it alone. His front foot is well behind the crease. Good discipline from him.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

FOUR! Almost another one! Gabriel comes from around the wicket and bowls a pinpoint yorker on off, Chisoro looks to jam it out but gets an inside edge past the off stump. The ball beats the diving keeper and races to the fine leg fence. Tendai is off the mark in Test cricket in a nervy manner.
Tendai Chisoro comes out to bat, it's his Test debut.

OUT! Gabriel was making the ball talk and he finally reaps the dividends! He steams in and hurls a fuller length ball outside off on a scrambled seam. After pitching, the ball keeps on coming in with the angle. Raza feels for it and gets a thick outside edge towards second slip. Kyle Hope stationed there takes it comfortably. Thankfully, for the Windies, he hasn't overstepped on this occasion. Raza departs after an enterprising knock. He would be disappointed to miss out on a ton.
Edged! Full length ball outside off, swinging away a touch. Raza pushes at it with minimal foot movement but gets an outside edge past the gully region for a couple.
Fractionally overpitched around off, Cremer puts in a nice stride forward and eases it to the cover region.
Straying on the pads, worked around the corner for a single.
Short delivery outside off, Sikandar goes for a pull across the line but gets foxed.

FOUR! All about timing and grace! Full length delivery in line of the stumps, Raza clips it beautifully through wide mid on. Chase gives it a chase from mid-wicket, looks to keep the ball in play but fails do so. He should have put in a slide there. Raza is now the leading run-scorer for Zimbabwe in Tests this year, going past Hamilton Masakadza.
On a length, shaping into Raza. He covers the line and defends it solidly.

That was not far away from the stumps! Good length delivery outside off, curving in. Raza lets it go and it just whizzes past the off pole. Both the new ball bowlers are extracting substantial movement from the deck.
Full delivery well outside off, the temptation is there to go for an expansive drive but Cremer resists. End of a probing over from Gabriel.

Gabriel is in good rhythm. He steams in and bowls a length delivery at 147 clicks outside off, gets it to seam in appreciably off the deck. Cremer knows where his off stump is and makes a confident leave.
Gabriel bowls this one fuller in length outside off, Cremer stays composed in his leave.
In the zone outside off, Graeme lets it go safely.

How did that miss the off stump? So, so close. Good length delivery in the corridor of uncertainty, Cremer opts to point his bat skywards as the ball nips back in substantially and just goes over the off stump. An older ball would have crashed into the stumps.
Full delivery outside off, Cremer strides forward and strokes it towards extra cover. Holder runs to his left, dives half-heartedly to his left and stops it partially. Two runs taken.
Short of a length outside off, holding its line. Raza doesn't flirt with it.
Angling in on a length from around off, Raza defends it solidly off the back foot.
Back of a length delivery just outside off, Sikandar makes good use of the depth of the crease and blocks it solidly.
Roach goes wide of the crease and hits the deck hard outside off, Raza points his bat skywards and allows it through.
FOUR! Well played! Fractionally overpitched outside off, Raza drills it through cover-point and the ball races to the fence. Good attacking batting from Sikandar.
Good length delivery in the zone of apprehension, Raza doesn't fiddle with it. The ball went on the bounce to the keeper.
Kemar Roach to share the second new ball from the other end. Two slips and a gully in place for him as well.
This time he angles in a short delivery from outside off, the skipper watches it closely and watches it sail through to the keeper.
Well-directed bouncer on middle and leg, Cremer sways away of the line of the delivery and drops his wrists to evade it.
Fractionally overpitched on off, Graeme leans into it nicely and punches it on the up to the mid on fielder.
Full delivery attacking the stumps, Cremer comes half-forward and plays it with an angled bat face to point.
Full length ball on middle and off, Sikandar clips it to fine leg for a single.
Good length delivery around off, Raza taps it besides the pitch on the off side and sets off for a run. The gully fielder comes charging in and so Cremer sends his partner back.

We are back for the afternoon session. The good thing is that the sun is out in all its glory at the moment. Sikandar Raza and Graeme Cremer to continue their innings. Shannon Gabriel to bowl first up after lunch. The second new ball has also been taken. Two slips and a gully in place.
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

Sikandar Raza has fought hard and already crossed the fifty-run mark. He has his skipper for company. Will they bat well and take the total in excess of 350 or will the visitors come out and wrap things up quickly? Join us in a while to find what happens next...

Session highlights - 39 Overs, 127 Runs and 3 Wickets! It's been a good extended session for both these sides. Zimbabwe continued to have the upper hand over the visitors with Masakadza and Raza churning the runs with ease in the first hour. Holder didn't opt for the second new ball and asked his spinners to bowl. Bishoo was way too short in his initial burst but once he pitched the ball up, he reaped huge dividends. Brathwaite from the other end offered him handy support as the duo extracted enough turn and bounce to cause panic in the opposition camp.
Fuller outside off, Raza drives it through covers to keep strike after LUNCH ON DAY 2!
Comes down the track. Kraigg pulls his length back. Raza adjusts and defends it.
Shorter in length outside off, the batsman pushes it on the off side for a run.
Quicker on off, turning back in. Cremer tries to work it on the leg side but gets an inside edge and on the bounce to short leg.
Flatter on off, Cremer defends it off the back foot.
A leg slip in place.
Advances down the track and drives it down to long on for a run.
Still a minute to go and we will have one more in before lunch...
Floats it on off, Cremer defends it off the front foot.
Goes onto the back foot and punches it through covers for a run.
Advances down the track, looses his balance in the process but Raza somehow manages to drives it back to the bowler.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Slower through the air on off, turning away. Cremer tries to defend but gets an outside edge towards short third man for a run.
A conversation between the two batsmen. Sikandar walks across to Cremer to have a word as he wants to eat up time and make sure that this is the last over before lunch.
Loopy ball on off, Raza drives it to the man at covers.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Floats it on off, Cremer defends it off the front foot.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A full toss on middle, Raza drives it down the ground for a run.
Cremer waits for the ball to spin into him and flicks it through square leg for a run.
Ambitious appeal but nothing from the umpire! Flatter on middle, turning back in. Cremer tries to defend but it goes off the pads to the man at short leg.
Slower through the air outside off, turning away. Raza tries to drive but gets beaten.

Cremer is off the mark! Short and wide outside off, from Bishoo. Graeme cuts it through point. The outfield is not that quick to take the ball to the fence. The fielder dives and pulls it back in to save a run for his side.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flatter on off, also shorter in length. Cremer defends it off the back foot.
Floats it up on off, Cremer defends it solidly.
Flighted ball outside off, Raza leans into it and drives it through covers for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flicks it to mid-wicket with the spin.
Dances down the track and times it through covers for a run.
Shorter in length outside off, Raza, against the spin, punches it through the cover region for a couple.
Quicker on leg stump, Raza flicks it to short leg.
Shorter in length on middle, turning back in. Raza works it to short leg.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Drags his length back outside off, Raza punches it through covers for a run.
FOUR! A gift by Bishoo! A full toss on middle, Raza goes down on one knee and sweeps it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
The batsman has driven that ball straight back.
Tosses it up on off, Raza defends it off the front foot.
Floats it wide outside off, Raza shoulders his arms to it.
Works it with the spin to mid-wicket.
Almost! Raza comes down the track and tries to drive the ball through the off side. The ball turns in sharply but luckily for Raza he gets an inside edge towards short fine leg for a run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Quicker on off, Raza defends it watchfully.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flatter on off, Raza defends it off the back foot.
Fuller outside off, Raza drives it down to long off for a run.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Tosses it up outside off, Raza pushes it to covers.

SIX! Fifty for Raza, his fifth in Tests! He brings it up in style! A long hop by Bishoo on middle, Raza goes back and picks the bones out of it as he deposits it over the mid-wicket fence. He is now Zimbabwe's only hope if they are to reach 350. He has played really well uptil now and he would want to make it count.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

NOT OUT! Cremer survives and the Windies lose a review! Brathwaite once again tosses it up outside off, this one too turns back in. Cremer prods forward to defend but gets beaten and is hit on the pads. The Windies appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Holder after a chat with his teammates opts to review. Replays show that there is not bat involved and the ball is spinning past the leg stump.
Review time! The Windies have taken a review for LBW against Cremer. Looks close!
Loopy ball outside off, turning back in. Cremer tries to defend but gets hit on the pads. The players appeal but the umpire remains put.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Floats it outside off, Raza drives it down towards mid off for a run.
Tosses it up on off, Raza defends it watchfully.
Flatter on off, Raza defends it off the back foot.
Graeme Cremer strides out to the middle.

OUT! BOWLED 'EM! 100 Test wickets for Bishoo, he becomes the 5th West Indian spinner to achieve this feat. Good variation from Bishoo! He pushes it quicker through the air, lands it full on middle. Chakabva goes down on one knee and tries to sweep but misses it completely. The ball goes between his legs and disturbs the woodwork behind. Chakabva's struggle comes to an end. Zimbabwe are losing their way now. Bishoo gets his second.
Sweeps it through square leg for a run.
The batsman has driven it straight back to the bowler.
BEATEN! It is turning square! Bishoo tosses it up on middle, the ball drifts into the batsman and turns away. Raza prods forward and tries to defend but gets beaten. A peach!
Drags his length back on off, Chakabva goes back and pulls it towards wide mid on for a run.
Tosses it up on middle, very full so the spin is out of contention. Raza drives it towards mid on for a run.
The batsman opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man. They pick up a single.
Flicks it to mid-wicket with the spin.
Quicker on the pads, Raza tries to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads.
Short and wide outside off, too easy for Chakabva. he is all the time in the world to rock back and cut it through point for three.
Flatter on middle, the batsman defends it by covering the line of the ball.
Tosses it up on off, Chakabva tries to defend but gets it off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
Shorter in length outside off, Raza shuffles across and flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Floats it up on off, turns away sharply. Raza gets beaten as he tries to defend it.
Flighted ball outside off, Raza need not play at it.
Slower through the air outside off, Raza lets it be.
Flatter on off, skids off the surface. Raza defends it towards covers.
Flighted ball on middle, Chakabva drives it towards mid on where Holder dives to his left and makes a good stop.
Flatter on off, the batsman defends stoutly.
Slower through the air, gets some turn off the surface. Chakabva tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Tosses it up on off, the batsman defends it off the front foot.
Flicks it with the angle to mid-wicket.
Advances down the track and drives it down to long on for a run.
Loopy ball outside off, Chakabva tries to sweep but gets beaten. A sweep shot against Bishoo, not a good idea.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter on off, turns away. Chakabva gets an outside edge down towards third man for a couple.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Floats it up outside off, Chakabva defends it off the front foot.

On middle and leg, Chakabva eases it down to long on for a single. But why is long on in place? Regis is the new man to the crease and why would you let him rotate strike? The man at long on should be brought up. This is really strange from Holder.
Shorter outside off, Chakabva punches it through the covers for a couple.

Brathwaite is getting some sharp turn here! He again slows it up outside off, turns back in and also skids off the surface. Chakabva goes back and tries to flick it but misses and is struck on the pads. The on-air commentators believe it was worth an appeal there. Replays show there was an inside edge there and maybe the keeper must have heard that.
Better this time! He bowls it slower through the air on off, Chakabva defends it solidly.
Quicker again on middle, Raza punches it down to long on for a run.
Flatter down the leg side, Raza tries to pull but misses.
Gives it air on off, turning away. Chakabva tries to defend but gets beaten.
Drives it with the spin to covers.
Fuller in length on the stumps, Raza drives it down to long on for a run.
Floats it outside off, Raza does not fiddle with it.

NOT OUT! Loopy ball outside off, turning away. Raza plays a similar shot like Masakadza but does not connect. The keeper collects and whips the bails off and appeals. The umpire goes upstairs. Replays show that Raza never lifted his foot.
An appeal for a stumping against Raza has been referred upstairs.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floats it full on off, the batsman drives it to mid on.
Loopy ball on off, turns back into the batsman. Chakabva tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Fuller outside off, Raza drives it through covers for a run.
Flatter on off, the batsman defends it off the back foot.
Sweeps it with the spin through square leg for a run.
Regis Chakabva is the next man in.

OUT! Waller bags a golden duck! An off spinner's dream delivery! The move of not taking the second new ball is paying off. Kraigg tosses it up outside off, inviting the batsman to drive. Waller obliges and tries to go through the line but leaves a gap between bat and pad. The ball turns in sharply and goes right between the gap to hit the timber. Two quick wickets for the Windies and they are ecstatic.
Drives it with the angle to mid on.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
Short again outside off, Raza cuts it through extra cover for a couple.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Malcolm Waller is the next man in.

OUT! This is what you get by bowling fuller! A loss of concentration from Masakadza, a bad shot by him. Not wise to go against the spin when the ball is turning. Bishoo again bowls a loopy ball outside off, turning away. Masakadza tries to fetch it and slog sweep it over the leg side but gets a top edge which lobs besides the pitch. Dowrich runs to his left, sets himself under it and takes it. A fighting innings by Hamilton comes to an end. He falls three short of his 150 and walks off to a standing ovation. West Indies have managed to break the 90-run stand and are now back into the game.

Nicely bowled! Bishoo tosses it up on middle, it drifts into the batsman, turns away sharply and also bounces extra. Masakadza goes on the back foot to defend but gets an outside edge through short third man for a couple.
Dances down the track and eases it down to long on for a single.
Allows the ball to turn in and works it towards mid-wicket.
Drops it on a length and it skids off the deck, HM does well to keep it out off the back foot.

A stifled appeal for an LBW! Pushes it quicker through the air around off, Masakadza tries to broom it away but misses and is struck on the pads. They appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Maybe, the impact would be outside the line.
A loopy full toss on middle, swept behind square on the leg side for a single. It was uppish but safe.
Very full around middle, bunted back to the bowler.

Kraigg Brathwaite is introduced into the attack. My colleague just reminded me that he was the one who removed Masakadza in the first innings of the first Test. Can he do it again? Well, his team would love it if he does so.
There you go! That is the length you need to bowl Bishoo! Floats it up around off, Hamilton leans forward to defend but the ball turns away and nearly kisses the outside edge of Masakadza's bat.
And again! Shortish around off, turning further away, punched towards Holder at short cover.
Ian Bishop is livid with the bowling from Bishoo. He wants him to bowl fuller and make the batsman come forward but Bishoo is bowling really flat and short.
What's with Bishoo? He is not learning. Continuously dropping it short and once again Raza cuts it to deep cover for a single.
Flatter one on the shorter length outside off, Masakadza smashes it through covers for a single.
Wide enough for the batsman to play at it.
Slower through the air outside off, spinning away further. The batsman lets it be.
Second new ball is due now!
Hamilton Masakadza now has the most number of runs in an innings for a batsman from Zimbabwe against West Indies in Tests.
Bouncer! the batsman ducks under it.
Better from Holder! He lands it on a length around off, Raza prods forward and blocks it.

FOUR LEG BYES! Poor by Holder! He errs in line and drifts it on the pads. Raza misses the flick as the ball brushes the pads, beats the diving keeper and into the fine leg fence. Second boundary of the over for Zimbabwe.
That was nicely timed as well but only for a single. Holder persists with the short ball on middle, Hamilton swivels inside the crease and pulls it to deep square leg for a run.

FOUR! Bad ball and it has been dispatched! Short and wide outside off by Holder. Seeing the width on offer, Massakadza goes after it and cuts it through backward point for a boundary. He moves onto 142.
Back of a length on off, Masakadza defends it off the back foot.
Ian Bishop on-air analyses his point further. The second new ball is around the corner and that will complicate issues for Bishoo. That is why he should have been bowled earlier in the morning.
Sixth short ball in a row, slapped hard but straight to the point fielder.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Bishoo hasn't got his rhythm. Drops it short again, punched off the back foot to sweeper cover for a run.
Short and spinning away, cut through point for a run.
Short again and Raza cuts it off the back foot to the cover region.
Starts off with a short delivery around off, cut past the diving cover fielder for a run.
Drinks time. Meanwhile, Devendra Bishoo is brought on for a bowl. Ian Bishop on-air feels that he should have been brought in earlier.
Drifting down the leg side, Raza looks to play it across but misses.
Leans into this one and pats it back to the bowler.
Floated outside off, Raza creams it to sweeper cover for a couple.

Missed opportunity! How costly will that be? Spinning sharply into Raza, he looks to tuck it across but seems to have got an inside edge on his pads. The ball lobs towards the short leg fielder who reacts very late. By the time he dives, the ball falls down on the ground. The Snicko confirms the inside edge. West Indies need to pounce on such opportunities if they are to come back in the game. This is a good track to bat on and the hosts can make you pay for it.
Lunges forward to this one and blocks it nicely.
Tossed up delivery, defended solidly off the front foot.

FOUR! Hit with disdain! Hamilton is showing his colorful array of shots all around the ground. Short delivery in line of the stumps, Masakadza swivels across and pulls it with aplomb through square leg for a rocketing boundary. Best over of the innings, 13 from it.
On a length outside off, holding its line. Hamilton doesn't fiddle with it.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Off pace delivery from Holder on a fullish length on middle, Masakadza is early into his drive and hence, gets it uppishly towards mid off. The fielder dives to his right but it goes past him. It rolls away on this slow outfield and through to the fence.

FOUR! An artist at work! Length delivery around off, Masakadza strides forward confidently and drives it through cover-point. Brathwaite in the deep runs to his right but the ball has been timed so well that it beats him with ease.
Angling sharply into Raza who works it to mid-wicket for a run.
Fullish delivery in the channel outside off, Raza watches it closely and makes a good leave.

FOUR! Nice improvisation! Floated around off, Masakadza goes for the fancy reverse sweep and executes it well. There is no protection in the deep behind square on the off side and he hits in the same region. Picks up another boundary.
Another one that spins down the leg side, Hamilton leaves it.
Clipped with the spin towards mid-wicket.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Tossed up around leg stump, Raza goes for the reverse sweep but misses to get hit around the hips. The ball deflects towards fine leg. Two leg byes taken.
Chase comes from around the wicket and bowls it around the pads, Raza looks to help it away but misses.
On a driving length outside off, Masakadza doesn't get drawn into the drive and lets it go safely.
In the off stump channel, Masakadza lets it go.
Back of a length delivery, angling in from outside off. Hamilton pushes it off the inner half of the bat towards mid on.
Fuller in length, defended solidly off the front foot.
Good length delivery around off, Raza hops and works it through square leg for a run. That brings up the 50-run stand between the two. They have shown good character and are playing really well.
Three slips in place now. West Indies on the attack.
On a length outside off, tapped past point for a single.
Floated delivery, Sikandar lunges forward and keeps it out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Tossed up delivery, Raza strokes it through covers. The fielder hares after it and cuts it off before the boundary ropes. Two runs taken. Actually, there was the third run on offer but poor running between the wickets didn't allow the batsmen to take it.
Spinning into Raza who clips it to short leg.
Raza turns this one with the spin towards mid-wicket.

FOUR! Picked the gap to perfection! Full toss on off, Raza kneels and sweeps it nicely past the short leg fielder. There are two men in the deep, one at deep square leg and one at long leg and he bisects them to earn a boundary. 200 up for Zimbabwe.
Stays back to this one and defends it. A maiden for Holder, testing over from him.

Ooh... that was close! Back of a length delivery angling in sharply from outside off, Masakadza looks to force it through covers with hard hands but gets a thick inside edge past the leg stump. He would have had his heart in his mouth there.
Fuller in length outside off, left alone.
In the zone of apprehension, Hamilton plants his front foot across and lets it go. These two have played sensible cricket, left deliveries outside the off stump and have played very few false shots.
Length delivery on off, Masakadza tucks it off the inner half of the bat to mid-wicket.
Back of a length delivery around off, Hamilton stays back and punches it back to the bowler.
Loopy delivery, Raza lunges forward in defense. Good over from Chase.
Quicker on middle, turned through mid-wicket for a single.
That was risky! Full delivery on middle, Masakadza goes for the fancy reverse sweep and connects decently to get it to short third man. If he missed that, he was a goner.
Strides forward to the tossed up delivery and defends it.

Nicely bowled! Chase spots Raza using his feet and bowls it slow through the air around off. Sikandar tries to push it through the gap at extra cover but gets beaten in the flight. Ends up getting an inside edge onto his pads and towards mid on. A run taken.
Short delivery around off, turning in slowly into Sikandar. He plays it with soft hands towards backward square leg for a single.
Well played! Length delivery just outside off, skidding after pitching. Raza shuffles a bit and keeps it out by taking his bottom hand off the bat.
In the channel outside off, curving in a touch. Sikandar doesn't flirt with it.
A touch fullish on off, Raza opts to stay back instead of coming forward and buries it into the track.
Raza taps this length delivery towards backward point and looks for a run but is rightly sent back.
Short of a length well outside off, Masakadza makes good use of the depth of the crease and punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
Good length delivery angling in from around off, Hamilton covers the line and answers it with a straight bat.
False start! Holder stops in his delivery stride.
The skipper, Jason Holder comes in for a burst.
FOUR! Pleasing shot! Half-volley outside off, Raza opens the face of the bat and drives it elegantly through covers for a boundary. 8 from the over.
Spinning into the pads, Sikandar helps it towards fine leg. Good running between the wickets allows the batsmen to come back for the second.
Fraction short around off, cut away against the spin to covers to rotate strike.
Turn on that occasion! Spins in sharply from outside off, Hamilton looks to defend it with the spin but is struck on the pads
Fullish on off, pushed off the front foot towards mid on.
Turning into Raza who turns it to mid-wicket for a run.
Roston Chase comes into the attack. He got good purchase from the track yesterday and will be looking to put pressure on the batsmen. A slip and short leg in place.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Hamilton presses forward and defends it solidly.
Much better this time. Fuller in length just outside off, the opener plants his front foot across and makes a good leave.
Gabriel loses his radar and slants it down the leg side, Hamilton tries to play it across but fails to put bat on ball.

Bouncer but wayward in direction. It is down the leg side, no trouble at all for Masakadza to leave it alone. A short delivery should be well-directed otherwise there is no meaning to the effort ball.
A tad fuller in length on off, Hamilton strides ahead and blocks it solidly towards Gabriel who mimes a throw to the keeper.
Straying on the hips, Raza turns it to fine leg for a run.
Roach goes wide of the crease and creates a testing angle. Gets the ball to come in substantially as Masakadza defends it tentatively from within the crease.
This time it is well outside off, Hamilton points his bat skywards to allow it through.
Back of a length outside off, Hamilton camps back and strokes it to the cover region.
Fuller in length this time, Masakadza presses forward and keeps it out.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, driven crisply to mid off.
Shuffles across to the good length delivery and turns it around the corner for a run.
As Ed Rainsford mentioned, the fielder in the leg side came into focus. Full length delivery on leg stump, flicked straight to the man who came in the mid-wicket region.
Down the leg side, Hamilton looks to play it across but misses it.

Ed Rainsford on-air mentions a good point. In the first Test match, the ball hardly traveled through the gully region. So, he adds that it is rather better to have a short leg in place. Let the batsman know that a bouncer might be coming up so keep them alert.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! Fullish and straying on the pads, Masakadza clips it with authority through mid-wicket. Chase hares after it but the ball wins the race this time.
Back of a length ball on off, Masakadza punches it firmly off the back foot to covers.
Shortish and room on offer, Hamilton slaps it hard but hits it straight to the man in the point region.

Good length delivery around off, Masakadza makes good use of the depth of the crease and taps it to the cover region. Gabriel is not looking his hundred percent. He was limping yesterday as well. Let's hope he is fine.
Alan Wilkins on-air mentions that Roach is quick off the pitch and has a habit of surprising the batsmen. It is not easy to get set against him. You have to be on your toes all the time.
Short delivery outside off, Raza lets it go.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Full delivery on middle, Raza pushes it off the inner half to mid on.
Another one in the channel outside off, Sikandar doesn't fiddle with it.
Good length delivery outside off, Sikandar leaves it alone in an awkward manner.

What a brute of a delivery! Cut into two halves! Roach goes wide of the crease and shapes in a pacy length delivery on off. Raza is caught in a tangle and gets beaten on the inside edge. The ball seems to have brushed the body and carries to Dowrich. Roach is confident but the keeper straightaway indicates that it came off the thigh pad. Raza is lucky to survive that one.
On a length on middle, Raza shuffles across and tucks it nicely to fine leg for a run and will retain strike.
Another short ball but the direction is wayward. It is down the leg side and Sikandar leaves it easily.
Good signs! Finally a bit of sun peeping through the clouds.
Well-directed bouncer on middle and leg, doesn't rise as much as expected. Raza has to duck under it in a jiffy to evade it.
Gabriel slips this one on the pads and Hamilton stays well balanced. He clips it beautifully through mid-wicket. Chase chases it on this slow outfield and cuts it off. Saves a run for his side.
Fractionally overpitched around off, timed sweetly to mid off.
Length delivery around off, Hamilton stays back and defends it stoutly.
Brave leave! Angling in prodigiously from outside off on a fuller length, Sikandar covers his off pole and lets it go. Good over from Roach.

Alan Wilkins on-air praises Roston Chase. He has played 14 Tests and scored a decent amount of runs (934) as well as picked up wickets (26). He is an underrated cricketer but he has a lot of potential which he proves time and again.
In the zone outside off, left alone.
In the off stump channel, a bit of nibble in the air. Raza knows where his off stump is and makes a good leave.
Roach searches for some swing and hence, bowls it fullish on off. Doesn't get much movement though and Raza deals with it easily.
Good length delivery around off, defended solidly off the back foot.
The sweeper cover comes in. Right tactic from Holder.
Full delivery on off, Hamilton crouches and taps it to mid on for a swift single.
Not much movement either in the air or off the pitch for Gabriel. On a length on off, holding its line. Sikandar gets behind the line of the delivery and eases it to covers.
Effort ball from Gabriel! He hits the deck hard and bowls it around off, Raza sways away from the line of the delivery, drops his wrists and makes a good leave.
A touch fuller this time but well outside off, Raza plants his front foot across and lets it go safely.
Full length delivery attacking the stumps, Sikandar prods forward and defends it with a high elbow.
Two slips for Raza.
Shaping into Hamilton who tucks it nicely through square leg to rotate strike.
Good length delivery in the corridor of uncertainty, angling in. Masakadza hangs back and defends it nicely to covers.
Shannon Gabriel to bowl from the other end. A slip and a gully in place. The slip fielder is standing in a much more conventional position for Gabriel.
Full delivery on the base of off stump, Raza leans ahead and blocks it solidly.
Two slips and a gully in place for Raza. West Indies are attacking him as he is new to the crease.
Stays back to this one and answers it with a straight bat.
Roach goes wider of the crease and angles in a full length delivery into Hamilton. He shuffles a bit and pushes it to mid off for a run.
Similar delivery outside off, not close enough to induce a stroke from Masakadza.
Length delivery in the zone of apprehension, a bit of inward movement. Masakadza points his bat skywards and allows it through.

FOUR! What a way to start off the day for Masakadza! Half-volley outside off, Hamilton leans ahead confidently and creams it past the diving extra cover fielder to find the fence. He is continuing from where he left off.

We are set to get rolling. The weather is a bit warmer this morning in Bulawayo. Hamilton Masakadza and Sikandar Raza to continue their innings. Kemar Roach to steam in with the ball. He got the rewards last morning. Can he get them today as well? A wide slip in place. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo says the pitch was covered due to the weather but there are some dry areas from which the ball might turn and bounce. Adds if the batsmen show some resistance they will be well on course to get a decent first innings total.

On the other hand, the tourists were more or less disciplined. They would be aiming to restrict the home side to as less as possible. With grey clouds looming overhead, it will be a stern test for the batsmen. Let's hope the rain stays away and we get in the allotted overs today.

Hello and a warm welcome to the coverage of Day 2 of the second and final Test between Zimbabwe and West Indies in Bulawayo. The hosts have shown that they have the temperament to bounce back from tough situations. Masakadza emerged as the hero for them as he scored an unbeaten century and is still going strong. However, he needs support from the lower middle order if they are to go past the 300-run mark.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Come the third session, Moor departed as soon as he scored a fifty but the onus was on Hamilton Masakadza who was approaching his Test ton. He got to it but then the dark clouds opened up, not allowing any more play. The conditions got very gloomy forcing the match officials to call it a day. The hosts would feel they have got out of the jail but the question is, will they be able to carry this further? With 29 overs getting lost today, the match will begin half an hour early, that is 0930 local for the next three days and it shall begin 5 minutes early, that is 0955 local on the final day to cover up for the time and overs lost. Do join us tomorrow to see how this Test pans out, weather permitting. Until next time, it's goodbye from us. Cheers!

A damp squib is what we got to witness after two good sessions of play today. After opting to bat on a chilly morning, Zimbabwe's top order was dented within no time as the Windies' pacers took full toll of the conditions that were on offer. They could have had even more had Gabriel not overstepped when Masakadza was batting on 15. Hamilton then got good support from Moor. The duo weathered the storm and staged a remarkable recovery. They kept the visitors at bay for the entire second session and in the process stitched a game-changing 142-run stand.
1646 local time update - And as expected, the conditions aren't deemed good enough for the play to continue and THAT'S STUMPS ON DAY 1!

1615 local time update - The rain has subsided a bit but there is still a light drizzle. Keeping that and light in mind, it seems like the inevitable is on the cards. But still let's wait for the official confirmation...

1555 local time update - The news isn't good, folks! The rain is only getting heavier and the entire ground is now covered. The light can be a issue too as it has gone all gloomy. Chances of further play look bleak but let's keep our fingers crossed...

1525 local time - Both the umpires come together to have a word as the drizzle has gotten heavier. It's quite murky as well. And they call for the covers now. The groundsmen coming running in. The players are asked to leave the field. Stay with us as we will keep you posted...
Gives this some more flight, Raza drives it back to the bowler.
Flighted delivery outside off, pushed back to the leggie.
Bishoo has bowled too many short balls today. Hamilton cuts it through backward point for a single.
Short outside off, punched through covers for a single.
It has started to drizzle now informs Ian Bishop on air...
Takes a stride forward and drives it towards cover.
Low full toss, dipping in, worked towards mid on.
Sikandar comes down the track to push it away but gets it off the outer half towards backward point for a quick single.
Turns in with bounce, Raza clips it past short leg.
Darted on middle, worked towards mid-wicket.

5th Test ton for Hamilton, second against the Windies! He gets there after being lucky earlier. He has made it count this time around and the crowd is up on its feet to laud the effort of this man. Entire Zimbabwe team is clapping for him in the dressing room. What a proud moment this is for him. He soaks in all the applause as he takes the helmet off and gets a hug from Raza. Coming to the ball, fuller ball on middle, driven past the bowler down the ground for a single.
Masakadza is on 99, the crowd is right behind him. Can he get there?
Floated delivery outside off, Raza comes down the track to drive but gets it off the inner half through mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up outside off, Maskadza comes forward and taps it towards the off side for a brisk single. On 99 now!
FOUR! What a hit! Bishoo once again bowls it short and was asking for trouble. Raza goes deep in the crease and cracks it through extra cover for a boundary to end the over.
Leans forward and blocks it out.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Short and outside off, Raza gets on top of the bounce and cuts it through cover-point for a couple.
Gets forward and strokes it straight to Holder at cover.
Fuller and wider on off, Hamilton pushes it towards backward point. There is a slight hesitation between the batsmen as to run or not and eventually decide to cross.
Sikandar Raza walks in next!

OUT! Bowled 'em! It's totally against the run of play! Roston Chase is the one who breaks the 142-run stand! The Windies are relieved at the moment as they have been kept at bay for a long period of time. Chase pushes it quicker through the air, drops it a touch short around off. Moor goes back to defend but this one skids off the surface, beats the outside edge and knocks the off stump. Moor can't believe it but has to walk back after playing a fine innings.
Flatter again on middle, Moor is right behind to keep it out.
Goes back to this flatter ball and defends it down.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Gets right forward and smothers it down.
Flighted full ball served outside off, Hamilton makes room to drive but gets a thick inside edge towards short fine leg for a single.
Floats it up outside off, blocked gently off the front foot.
Short and outside off, cut past the man at point for a single.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Fuller on off, driven towards the man at extra cover.
Flighted delivery around middle, Masakadza makes room to drive but gets a thick inside edge on the pads.
Bowls it well outside off, left alone.
Goes back and punches it towards cover.

FOUR! There it is, 3rd Test fifty for Peter Moor! He came into the side as a replacement and has grabbed the opportunity with both the hands. The fact that he walked in when his side was in early trouble will make this fifty even more special for him and his side. Coming to the ball, a full toss outside off, Moor leans ahead and drives it through covers. Blackwood sprints after it but the ball still wins the race.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Flatter delivery on middle, tucked off the back foot towards the leg side.
Flighted delivery outside off, driven down to long off for a single.
Takes a stride forward and nudges it towards short mid-wicket.
Loops it up outside off, Moor goes back to cut but mistimes it towards the cover fielder.
Tossed up outside off, eased down to long off for one.
Short on middle, punched down to long off for a single.
Bishoo once again drops it short, it turns away, cut away towards the fielder at extra cover. Moor is not happy, he knows that he should have put that away.
Short and outside off, cut away towards extra cover.
Fuller outside off, driven straight to the cover fielder.
Devendra Bishoo to bowl from the other end...

What is Masakadza doing? Once again tires to play the reverse sweep but gets hit on the pads. Getting a bit fidgety here is Hamilton. Replays show it did take some part of the gloves before dying down.
Quicker delivery around middle and leg, Hamilton prods forward to defend but gets it off the pads towards short fine leg.
Full outside off, blocked off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up ball outside off, Masakadza tries to reverse sweep this but the ball turns in and he gets beaten.
Flatter ball on middle and off, crunched off the back foot towards point.
Bowls it around leg, it turns further down, the batsman lets it be.

Welcome back for the final session, folks! Hamilton Maskadza and Peter Moor stride out to bat. All eyes on the former as he is just 7 short of the three-figure mark. Roston Chase to continue the proceedings. Let's play...
... Day 1, Final session ...

The Windies will be really kicking themselves to have let the momentum slip away.  Gabrile overstepped when Masakadza was on 15 has come down as a haunting for them. In this session their bowlers apart from Roach looked off color. Bishoo and Chase are getting the ball to turn but they have bowled too many loose deliveries as well. Can they break this stand? Will we see Masakadza reaching the three-figure mark? Join us in a while to find out...

What a session for Zimbabwe, a wicket-less one! They were down and out in the morning, losing three quick wickets but since then Hamilton Masakadza and Peter Moor have done a really good job to hold the innings together. Agreed, the former got a few lives but he has made it count. The latter looked a bit desperate to score runs but his side will be happy to see him still out there. The stand is worth 133 and it will be interesting to see if these two can swell it to a big one.
Edgyyy! Tossed up ball outside off, Moor leans ahead to drive but gets a thick outside edge which rolls past the slip fielder. They take two and that is TEA ON DAY 1!
Turning away from a length outside off, left alone.

In the air... safe! There is no need to go after this Moor. Really a bad approach with the tea break around the corner! Flighted delivery around middle, Moor gets down and goes for the slog sweep against the spin. The ball turns away and hence he gets a big top edge. However, there is no one patrolling in the deep mid-wicket region and so a couple is taken.
Bishoo drops it short outside off, turning away as well, slapped off the back foot through covers for a couple.
Flighted ball but a bit too full, driven through extra cover for one.
Tossed up delivery around off, defended off the front foot.
Flatter through the air, Moor goes back and tucks it on the bounce towards short leg.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. They pick up a single.

Almost... Chase is bowling really well! He is not afraid to flight the ball and is getting nice assistance off the deck too. Masakadza leans forward to defend but the ball turns in with some bounce and goes off the gloves towards short leg. Luckily for Hamilton it dies down well in front of the man there.
Floats it up outside off, blocked into the ground gently.
Shorter around off, defended off the back foot.

Chase slows it through the air outside off, Masakadza goes at it with hard hands, gets a thick inside edge on the boots as the ball lobs up towards the vacant silly point region. The man in the slip, Blackwood was interested but it was far away from his reach.
Lands it on middle, turning away, punched off the back foot towards cover.
Flatter delivery on middle, played back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Loopy delivery on off, pushed off the front foot towards cover.
Flighted delivery around off, driven through cover for one.
Tossed up on the stumps, Hamilton makes room and drives it through extra cover. Immediately calls for two and gets it comfortably.
Masakadza goes back and flicks it through mid-wicket and will keep strike.
Fuller on middle, wristed uppishly towards mid-wicket.
Quicker one on middle, defended off the back foot.
Roston drops it short on middle, tucked with the spin through backward square leg for a single.
Loopy delivery outside off, defended into the ground.
Darts it on middle and leg, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Driven straight to the cover fielder.
Quicker through the air outside off, Moor lets the ball go.
Comes forward and blocks it out.
Loopy leg-break outside off, Moor comes forward to defend but the ball turns away to beat the outside edge.
Once again it's outside off, nicely left alone.
Flatter outside off, left alone.
Devendra Bishoo is brought back into the attack.

NOT OUT! The on-field call has to be overturned! The crowd goes wild, they want to see the ton from the bat of Masakadza! Chase floats it up outside off, Hamilton dances down the track but the ball turns in and it goes off something to the short leg fielder. They all appeal and umpire Dharmasena raises his finger. Masakadza after taking his time challenges the decision. Front foot is fine. There is no spike on the Ultra Edge as the ball went past the bat. So, maybe it came off the forearm. Now they also check for the LBW and replays show the impact is miles outside off. Right then, Masakadza gets another life.

Hamilton Masakadza is given out caught at short leg. Now then, he walks towards Moor, takes his time and then opts for the review. He says, he isn't sure. Let's wait and find out. He is on 86, can he survive?
Top edge! Floats it up outside off, Moor gets down to sweep but gets a safe top edge over the keeper for a single.
Gets back to defend but once again is beaten by the turn and bounce and wears it on the pads.
Gets right behind the line and blocks it out watchfully.
Chase drops it short around middle, it turns in. Moor looks to turn it away on the leg side but gets it off the pads towards first slip.
Flighted delivery outside off, Peter Moor lunges forward to defend but there is some turn which takes the inside edge and dribbles between the legs towards short fine leg.
Jason Holder is back on the field and now Shannon Gabriel is walking off...
Once again it's on the shorter side outside off, HM lets it sail over him to the keeper.
Hits the deck hard on middle and off, Hamilton stands tall offers a straight blade.
Full toss on the pads, quelled into the leg side for a single.
Jason Holder is off the field!
Gabriel goes wide of the crease and angles one on a fuller length, Moor bunts it back to the bowler.
Angles in a fuller length delivery on middle, defended nicely off the front foot.

FOUR! Ahhhh... that almost carried all the way! This is such a good shot to watch! Gabriel bowls a short of a length outside off, Moor stands tall, arches back just a touch and then as the ball arrives his ramps it over the keeper for a one bounce boundary.
This one turns in, Hamilton comes forward to defend but the ball goes off the pads and dies down in front of short leg.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Slows it through the air around middle, defended watchfully.

SIX! He has sent it out of the park! What a meaty blow, that! Chase gives it a nice flight outside off, Masakadza gets down on one knee and murders the slog sweep over deep mid-wicket for a biggie all the way. 2000 Test runs for this man!
Gets on the front foot and buries it into the ground.
Loopy delivery around off, defended off the front foot gently.
Stands tall and blocks it out back to the bowler. Gabriel mimes a throw and gives a stare to Moor. He looks really annoyed, understandably so but he has only himself to blame.
Fuller delivery outside off, driven with an open face bat towards point where Hetmyer (sub) dives full length to his left to stop some runs.
Change of bat for Peter Moor...
Fuller and tries to attack the stumps, Moor makes room and defends it back to the bowler.
Digs in a short ball, angling in on the body, the batsman ducks under it.
Back of a length delivery outside off, stabbed towards point.
Length delivery, angling in on middle, tucked through square leg for a single.
Tossed up delivery around middle, flicked towards the man at short mid-wicket.
Masakadza chips this over mid on and picks up a single.
FOUR! He has drilled it! Floated delivery outside off, Masakadza takes a stride forward and absolutely drills it through extra cover for a boundary. Booming shot, that!
Loopy ball outside off, defended once again off the front foot.
Keeps it a bit full this time, Masakadza comes nicely forward to counter the spin.
Floats it up outside off, it turns back in with some bounce as Hamilton punches it back to the bowler.
Roston Chase is brought into the attack now. Can he get a breakthrough?
Ends the over with a bouncer! Good amount of bounce but wasn't that threatening enough. Peter calmly ducks under it.
Drifting on the pads, clipped down to deep backward square leg for a single.
What was that? On a length and outside off, this one holds its line as Masakadza initially tries to play at it but then makes a leave at the very last moment.
Keeps it full again around that off stump line, Hamilton drives it to the left of Gabriel who collects and mimes a throw.
Touch fuller and angling in, bunted back to the bowler.

100-run stand comes up! Short of a length delivery on middle and leg, Moor swivels a touch and pulls it with control down to fine leg for a single. These two have put up a good show so far. How long can they continue?
Wider outside off, Moor unfurls a classic cover drive to keep strike.
Short of a length delivery on middle, tucked towards square leg for nothing.
This is wayward! Holder once again bangs in a short ball but well down the leg side, Moor leaves it alone.
Bangs in a short ball on middle, Moor at the last moment ducks under it.
Length delivery around middle and off, defended off the back foot.
Holder comes from around the wicket, angles it away on a fuller length outside off, driven wide of mid off for a couple of runs.
Good length delivery just outside off, Masakadza shuffles a touch and answers it with a straight bat.
Sharp bouncer on leg stump, Hamilton ducks under it in a jiffy.
Full length delivery on middle, pushed off the inner half of the bat to deep backward square leg. A run taken.
Angling into Hamilton who nudges it to wide mid on to rotate strike.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Half-volley around off, Masakadza strides ahead and eases it past Gabriel. The swing of the bat was nice and the timing was spot on. The ball whistles away to the fence.
Good length delivery on off, Masakadza blocks it off the back foot. That hit the bat hard.
In the zone of apprehension, Moor doesn't flirt with it.
Back of a length outside off, punched firmly off the back foot. Moor calls his partner through for a run and completes it with ease.
Length delivery around off, Hamilton hangs back and blocks it solidly.
Tucks Moor with a shortish delivery around the rib-cage area. He fends it away around the corner for a run.
Another one in the channel outside off, Peter plants his front foot across and lets it go.
Fullish delivery outside off, Moor points has bat skywards to allow it through.

A bit of an issue with the ball again. The leather needs trimming. Meanwhile, the umpires call for drinks. Zimbabwe have recovered really well after the initial jolt. Masakadza and Moor are going along nicely and have also punished the loose deliveries. The Windies need to give their best to dislodge this partnership. Meanwhile, the umpires are sipping a cup of coffee in this chilly weather.
Short of a length delivery, Masakadza rises with the bounce and taps it besides the pitch on the off side.
FOUR! Nicely done! Fullish delivery just outside off, Masakadza drives it with a high elbow past Gabriel down the ground. Holder gives it a chase from mid off but only comes second best.
A man at sweeper cover in place now.
Good early call! Taps the fullish delivery to covers and calls his partner through for a run. Masakadza is running to the danger end but beats the throw with ease.
A bit wider outside off, Moor isn't bothered to play at that one.
Overpitched outside off, Peter leans into it and strokes it to Brathwaite at extra cover.
Full length delivery on off, eased past the bowler. Gabriel is limping in his followthrough. He has had his issues with his hamstring and needs to be careful. He is fine to continue at the moment.
It is extremely cold. Tough day for the crowd as well. People are wrapped in their blankets and have scarves around their neck. Meanwhile, Shannon Gabriel returns for a bowl.
Back of a length outside off, blocked solidly off the back foot.
On a length around off, angling into Masakadza. He hangs back to defend it but gets an inside edge onto his thigh pad and the ball deflects towards the slip region.
Good running! Moor strides forward confidently and strokes it to mid off for a swift single.
Leans ahead to the fullish delivery and caresses it to the fielder in the cover region.
Length delivery well outside off, holding its line. Peter doesn't flirt with that one.
On a fuller length outside off, curving in. Moor plants his front foot across and makes a watchful leave.
Quicker outside off, left alone watchfully.
FOUR! A bish from Bishoo! Short ball around off, Masakadza waits in the crease and just picks it up over mid on to find the fence. The spinner is looking a bit off colour in this cold weather.
Shortish this time, punched off the back foot through extra cover. The fielder in the deep hares to his left and cuts it off. A brace taken.
Pushed to mid off from the front foot.
Similar delivery, mistimed drive back to the bowler.
Tossed up outside off, Hamilton leans into it and strokes it to mid off.
Shortish delivery around off, Peter sways away from the line of the delivery, drops his wrists and lets it sail into the gloves of the keeper.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, pushed off the front foot to the cover region.

Half-volley outside off, Moor opens the face of the bat and drives it through point. Blackwood hares after it from backward point and saves a couple for his side. He is lightning quick across the turf.
Full delivery attacking the stumps, played with soft hands to mid-wicket.
On a length in the corridor of uncertainty, Peter points his bat skywards to let it be.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Moor backs away and defends it besides the pitch on the leg side.
A bit of leather is coming out from the ball. The umpire cuts it off and we are ready to go again.

SIX! Where did that come from? Really well played! Short delivery well outside off, Masakadza hangs back and hammers it over wide long on for a maximum. It is a long boundary there and he clears it with ease.
Tossed up around off, spinning away. Hamilton leaves it alone.
Quicker in pace, pushed back to the bowler.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single.
Moor stays back and punches it to the same fielder.
Floated delivery on off, driven with the spin to short extra cover.
Another one outside off and Hamilton doesn't fiddle with it.
Stays back to the good length delivery and buries it into the ground.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Hamilton drops his wrists and gets a bit of glove on it. The ball bounces and goes towards the keeper.

FOUR! 8th Test fifty for Hamilton Masakadza! Short delivery in line of the stumps, Masakadza pulls it with authority through backward square leg. Right in the gap between the two fielders in the deep and he picks up another boundary. It has been a measured knock from him. He was out off a no ball but has since then, looked assured and needs to carry on.
Good length delivery outside off, shaping in substantially. Masakadza trusts his judgement of where his off stump is and makes a good leave.
Jason Holder is back into the attack.
Another one spinning away from Peter and he doesn't fiddle with it.
Outside off, Moor leaves it alone.
Short delivery, cut with the spin to the point region.
Flat and quick, punched off the back foot to short cover.
Continues to be short, this time it is punched with the spin to point.
A bit short on off, Masakadza makes good use of the crease and cuts it to deep cover-point. A run taken.
Full length delivery attacking the base of off stump, Moor puts his head down and pushes it to mid off.
Waits for this one and taps it with an open face of the bat to point.
Roach goes wider of the crease and bowls a full delivery around off, driven firmly off the front foot to mid off.
Fullish delivery angling in from around off, blocked solidly by covering the line of the ball.
Overpitched around off, driven crisply to sweeper cover for a brace.

Fuller in length around off, Moor chooses to stay back and defend it. Ian Bishop on-air mentions that in Roach's previous over, an edge went past the second slip region. He feels that is the reason the first slip fielder has been moved wider.
Well outside off, Hamilton shuffles across his stumps and leaves it.
Lunges forward to this one and defends it.
Another edge! Around off, Masakadza pushes at it with hard hands and gets an outside edge past first slip. Two runs taken.
Skidding off the surface and in line of the stumps, Hamilton blocks it watchfully.
Short around off, Masakadza pushes at it but gets it off the outer half through short third man. Chase chases it from backward point and saves a couple for his side.
Floated delivery, eased with the spin to short extra cover.
Full length delivery attacking the stumps, Moor clears his front leg and looks to jam it out but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Fullish on middle and leg, Moor looks to clip it away but is struck on the thigh pad. A casual appeal is turned down. It was always heading down leg.
Bouncer around off, Moor sways away from the line of the delivery to evade it. It dies on the keeper. Indications that it is an abrasive surface.
Good length delivery shaping into Moor. He keeps it out off the inner half of the bat.
On a length outside off, holding its line. Peter doesn't fiddle with it.

Ian Bishop on-air mentions that short leg can be brought in place. Roach is getting good inward movement and that might induce a false stroke towards that region. It is about applying mental pressure as well.
Good length delivery outside off, seaming in sharply. Moor covers the line and blocks it down the track.
Tossed up on off, knocked down to long off for a single.
Played with the spin to the point region this time.
Well outside off, Moor lets it go.
Shortish again, Hamilton cuts it through cover-point for a singe.
Fraction short this time, punched with the spin to short extra cover.
Full delivery around off, Masakadza goes for the sweep against the spin but gets it off the inner half to fine leg. Two runs taken.
Tailing in nicely on a fullish length, Peter closes his bat face early and hence, gets an inside edge onto his boots as the ball deflects to the short cover region. Another good over.
Overpitched outside off, driven sweetly to the man in the cover region.
Roach is getting good movement. Swinging in from around off, Moor covers the line and plays it defensively to mid-wicket.
Roach again goes wider of the crease and angles in a length delivery. Moor pushes at it tentatively but gets a thick inside edge to mid-wicket.
Shortish delivery and room on offer, punched on the up to sweeper cover to rotate strike.

Full delivery tailing into Masakadza who clips it nicely through mid-wicket. Two runs taken. That brings up the 50-run stand between the two. An important partnership, they have played sensible cricket and need to carry on.
Tossed up delivery, defended solidly off the front foot. Good over from Bishoo.
Bishoo is making an impact straightaway! Quick and flat on off, Moor prods forward to defend but is beaten by the sharp turn.
Around off, Moor covers his stumps and lets it go.
Poor shot! Tossed up around off, Moor kneels and goes for a slog sweep across the line but gets a top edge over second slip. Two runs taken. Moor needs to be careful.
Outside off, spinning away. Moor leaves it alone.
Quick through the air on off, kept out watchfully.
Bishoo to continue his spell. Two slips in place.
Shaping in sharply from a length around off, Masakadza is cramped for room and blocks it towards mid on.
Ed Rainsford on-air mentions that Masakadza has done well to leave the balls outside the off stump. His teammates were guilty of fiddling with deliveries in that channel and paid the price for it.
Good length delivery outside off, left alone.
Around the hips, tucked to fine leg for an easy single.
Roach goes wider of the crease and angles in a full length ball on off, Peter drives it crisply to wide mid off.
Length delivery outside off, Moor doesn't fiddle with it.
Well bowled! Cross seam delivery on a back of a length on off, Moor is taken aback by the sharp bounce and gets a thick outside edge in the gap between slip and gully. Two runs taken.

No ball! Starts off with a high full toss, a beamer. Masakadza keeps it out around the corner for a run. Roach immediately apologizes to him, that was not intentional. If he bowls another one, he will be taken out of the attack.
We are back for the afternoon session. Hamilton Masakadza and Peter Moor to continue batting. Kemar Roach to bowl first up after lunch. A wide slip in place. Here we go...
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

The pair of Masakadza and Moor though has stitched a decent partnership to get things going or the matters could have been worse. Remember, Gabriel also got a wicket off a no ball of Masakadza. He needs to address his front foot issue sooner rather than later. Zimbabwe will look to get back into the contest while the tourists will be eager to keep taking wickets. Holder gave only one over to Bishoo and we might see him bowling a lot in the second session. Join us in a while.

Great opening session of the game for the Windies. Grey clouds are still looming overhead and the visitors have made the most of the conditions on offer. Both Gabriel and Roach were on the money and took three quick wickets to put the hosts on the back foot. There was no real application from the Zimbabwean batsmen and that led to their downfall.
Tossed up outside off, left alone by Moor. Good over by Bishoo, a maiden. That's Lunch, Day 1!

Nicely bowled! Bowls it outside off, with a bit of drift, Moor looks to defend but is beaten all ends up. The batsman did lose his balance in the process but thankfully for him, he never left the crease and hence could not be out stumped.
Floated outside off, driven towards covers by Moor.
This one is wide enough for the batsman to leave it.
Flights it outside off, Moor pushes it towards covers.
Loops it outside off, driven towards covers by the batsman.
As expected, Devendra Bishoo comes on for a bowl. Last over of the session too...
Shorter in length from Holder, Hamilton pulls it through square leg for a couple of runs.
Full and outside off, driven towards covers by Masakadza.
Good length outside off, left alone.
Full and straight on the stumps, driven towards mid on by the batsman.
Angles a good length ball around off, defended watchfully. Holder screams in disgust as he is not happy with himself.
Shorter in length outside off, Masakadza pulls it to the right of Blackwood at short mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Full and outside off, Moor defends it towards point from his crease.
Gabriel bowls this full and this time he gets Moor to poke at it. The ball swings away and beats the bat. Moor was playing for the one that comes into the batsman.
Same line, same length, same shot by the batsman.
Full and outside off, left alone by the batsman.
Gabriel bowls it outside off on a fuller length, Moor is not bothered.
Bishoo is warming up.... Might have him bowling in the first session soon. Could be as early as the next over.
Shorter in length outside off, Moor backs away and pats it towards point.
Shorter in length outside off, punched into the off side by the batsman.
Full length outside off, left alone by Moor.

Fazeer Mohammed on-air mentions that Zimbabwe need to play more Test cricket. This is their third Test match this year while the other teams have played much more. Bangladesh had got their opportunities and they have improved as a side. The ICC should take steps to give the African nation more opportunities to prove their worth.
Hurls a length ball just outside off, Moor comes forward to defend but gets an inside edge through the leg side for a single.
Angles a length ball outside off, swings in, left alone.
Similar length just around off, Moor defends it from his crease.
Good length outside off, Moor is not interested.
Angles a full length ball around off, Hamilton comes forward and blocks it.
Good length outside off, left alone.
A sweeper goes back.

FOUR! Good shot! Full and outside off, Masakadza strides forward and drives it through the covers. This time the timing is good and he gets a boundary, which is a rare thing on this slow outfield. 50 up for the home side.
Angles a length ball just around off, Masakadza defends it from his crease.
Good length outside off, defended towards covers.
Good length outside off, left alone.
Shannon Gabriel returns for a burst.
Good length outside off, Moor thinks of playing at it and nearly does so before withdrawing his bat at the last moment.
Shorter in length outside off, pulled through mid-wicket for a single.
Shorter in length outside off, Masakadza drops his wrists and lets it go.
Shorter in length outside off, punched towards point by the batsman.
Length ball outside off, left alone.

Jason Holder is missing a trick probably. He is still sticking with Jermaine Blackwood even though he is not posing any real threat to the batsmen. Agreed that the conditions are overcast but the go-to-man, Devendra Bishoo needs to be introduced into the attack. Zimbabwe are three down for not many and the pressure needs to be applied at this point of the game.
Good length outside off, no shot offered by Masakadza.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
Angles a length outside off, PJ Moor comes forward and defends it.
Beaten! Shapes it into the batsman from outside off, the ball pitches and goes away to beat the bat of Moor poking at it. Good ball, that.
Hurls it outside off on a length outside off, Moor mistimes his push into the off side.
Angles it on a length around middle, Masakadza shapes to turn it through the leg side but gets a soft leading edge towards mid off for a single.
Shorter in length outside off, punched on the up towards covers.
Back of a length outside off, Moor stands tall and defends it back down the wicket.
Thumped! Good length outside off, punched through the point region. Blackwood gives it a chase and saves two runs for his side.
Ouch! Banged in short around middle, Moor arches back and lets it go. The ball brushes the right shoulder of the batsman and goes towards the slip cordon. No appeal since there was no bat there.
Angles a length ball around off, Moor gets in line and defends it.
Holder goes full but too straight. Moor pushes it down the ground. The mid on fielder hares after it and cuts it off. Two runs taken thanks to the slow outfield.
FOUR! Smacked! Short and wide from Holder, Moor does not miss out and crashes it past point for a boundary. That is where he likes it and the Windies are not bowling to their plans at the moment.
Fuller in length, played back to the bowler.
This one is wide outside off, left alone.
Angles it on the pads, turned through the square leg region for a couple of runs.

NOT OUT! Weird! Fuller in length from Blackwood outside off, Masakadza drives it back down the wicket. Jermaine gets a hand to it and deflects it at the stumps at the bowler's end. The umpire is jumping to save himself but the ball still hits him on the neck. Fry the umpire refers it upstairs as he clearly had no time to see what transpired there. Replays show that Moor never left the crease and hence it is not out. Close call for the umpire there.

Wow! What happened there? Masakadza drives one back to Blackwood who manages to get a hand to it in his followthrough as the ball disturbs the stumps at the other end. The bowler is ringing his right hand as he appeals and umpire Simon Fry refers it upstairs...
A tad short around off, punched towards covers.
Bowls it outside off on a fuller length, left alone by the batsman.
Good timing! Overpitched outside off, Moor just pushes at it and gets it through the cover region. Two runs taken.
In the zone outside off, left alone.
Outside off, Moor is no mood to flirt with it. Alan Wilkins on-air informs that it is a really cold morning in Bulawayo. The players in the dressing room have their hands in the pockets.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Peter points his bat skywards to allow it through..
Holder loses his radar and slips this one down the leg side, Peter goes for the clip but misses.
Length delivery around off, shaping in. Moor has his off stump covered and makes an easy leave.
Back of a length delivery, Masakadza makes use of the depth of the crease to block it solidly.
In the channel outside off, Hamilton lets it go.
Full delivery outside off, Hamilton drives it with hard hands but once again fails to find the gap through the cover region.
Back of a length ball, helped to mid-wicket.
Gets nicely forward to this one and strokes it to covers.
Overpitched well outside off, Masakadza drives it nicely to mid off.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Moor lets it go.
Holder pitches it up this time, Moor puts his head down and defends it calmly.
Slanting down the leg side, Moor goes for the flick but misses
Fullish ball outside off, Peter doesn't fiddle with it.
Fullish delivery, defended solidly off the front foot to covers.
On a length outside off, left alone.
Holder comes in for a bowl.
Short of a length, pushed to mid off.
FOUR! Well played! Shortish and room on offer, Masakadza slaps it through point. The fielder from sweeper cover races to his left and slides but fails to stop it from crossing the ropes.
Fullish on off, eased to mid on.
Another nervy moment! Full outside off, Masakadza pushes at it but gets a bottom edge. The ball runs past the off stump and rolls towards Dowrich.
Back of a length outside off, punched through covers for a run.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Jermaine Blackwood comes into the attack. Might be only one over for the part-timer.
In the air... but safe! Full length delivery on off, Hamilton pokes at it but gets an outside edge that falls well short of Dowrich. Playing with soft hands was the key there.
Fullish delivery, pushed back to the bowler.
FOUR! Crisp! Back of a length delivery and width on offer, Masakadza frees his arms and slaps it through cover-point and the ball races to the fence.
Full delivery on off, Masakadza drives it straight to Roach who parries it with a half-stop to mid on.
Stays back to the length delivery and blocks it.
Fullish delivery outside off, Moor pushes at it but gets an inside edge to mid-wicket. A run taken.
Full length delivery attacking the stumps, driven sweetly to mid on.
Drinks.

WICKET OFF A NO BALL! Oh no! The perennial problem of Gabriel returns to haunt him again. He bowls the effort ball on a shorter length around off, Masakadza goes for a pull but seems to have edged it onto his right arm. The ball lobs in front of the slip cordon. Kyle Hope from gully runs across to his left and dives to take it really well. The players appeal vociferously but the umpire shakes his head. The visitors challenge the decision immediately. The opener starts to walk back but is asked to stop by the umpire. Time for the replays and Gabriel has overstepped. That's the end of the story. The Snicko spotted the edge. Hamilton gets another chance. Wonder how Gabriel is feeling right now! Replays show that he was flabbergasted. No review lost since it was a no ball.
Windies go for the review straightaway. They feel that there is certainly an edge as opposed to the umpire, Simon Fry. Let's find out..
Off-cutter on a fuller length just outside off, Masakadza spots it and drives it crisply to mid off.
Full length ball around off, Hamilton comes forward and eases it to covers.
Fullish delivery outside off, Masakadza strides forward and lets it go.
Short of a length outside off, Hamilton punches it through cover-point for a couple.
Gabriel is making the ball talk! Shaping in substantially from around off, Moor pushes at it tentatively and gets it off the inner half to fine leg. A run taken.
Stays back to the good length delivery and blocks it. Another productive over for the visitors.
